transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. To start off, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Well, I guess what finally made me come in is that my appetite has just been all over the place for months now. There are stretches where I just skip dinner entirely, and I've lost some weight without really trying to. And then other nights, I'll just pick at crackers or have a bowl of cereal... mostly because the thought of actually cooking a real meal for myself just feels completely pointless.
Over these past few months, have you also been feeling down, sad, or like you've lost interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy?

Yes, I suppose I have. I mean, I still try to go through the motions of the things I used to love doing. I'll go out to water the garden, or I'll make myself show up to my book club... but most of the time, it just feels really flat. I don't really get anything out of it anymore, so I usually end up leaving early, or sometimes I just don't even start at all.
How long has this low, flat feeling and loss of interest been going on for?
It started right around the time my divorce was finalized. So, that would be about a year and seven months ago now.

Since this started about 19 months ago, have you had any breaks—say, two months or longer—where you felt back to your normal self, or has this low, flat feeling been pretty much constant since the divorce?
No, there really haven't been any breaks. It's just been a constant, low feeling the whole time. I haven't had a period where I felt like my normal self since it all started.

During this 19-month period, has there been any stretch of time where your mood or symptoms became noticeably more intense or severe than the rest of the time, or has it felt like a steady, unchanging level the whole way through?

No, not really. It's... it's just been pretty steady, like you said. I mean, sure, some days might feel a little harder than others, but there hasn't been any specific stretch of time where it got noticeably worse or more intense. It's just been that same flat feeling the whole way through.
During this time, have you noticed any changes in your sleep, such as trouble falling asleep, waking up frequently, or sleeping much more than usual?

I don't really have trouble falling asleep—I can usually get into bed at a reasonable hour. But I've been waking up around four in the morning. My mind just starts going, thinking about bills, or my work notes, or the divorce. And then I just lie there... I'm completely exhausted, but I can't get back to sleep before the alarm goes off.
Have you had any thoughts of hurting yourself or that you'd be better off dead, and has this low mood made it hard to keep up with your daily responsibilities like work or household tasks?

I don't have any plan to hurt myself. But... I do sometimes catch myself thinking that it would just be a relief not to wake up. It actually scares me a bit to admit that, because I know I would take that very seriously if one of my clients said it to me. 

As for my daily responsibilities, I'm still managing to keep up with my work and things around the house, it just takes a lot more effort to push through it.
Over these past several months, have you been feeling unusually tired or low on energy, even when you haven't done much?

Yes, definitely. Even on days when my caseload isn't unusually heavy, I just feel like... I feel like I'm dragging my body through the hospital. It just takes so much effort to keep moving. And then when I finally get home, I'm completely drained. I'm too tired to cook, or do my stretches, or... or even answer personal messages on my phone. I just don't have the energy for any of it.
Have you noticed any changes in your ability to concentrate or make decisions, like at work or when reading?

Yes, I have. At work, especially during case reviews, I find myself having to reread the same notes several times because the information just isn't sinking in. And making decisions has gotten strangely difficult. Even simple things... like trying to decide which client call I need to return first, or just figuring out what to buy for dinner. It takes me an embarrassing amount of time to figure it out lately.
Have you been feeling unusually worthless or excessively guilty about things, even minor things, during this time?

Yes, I have. Mostly when it comes to my marriage. I just keep replaying it in my head, and... I keep telling myself that I must have failed at something really basic. Even though part of me knows relationships are a lot more complicated than that, I just can't seem to shake this heavy sense of guilt about it.
